_comment: The toolset that DESCRIBES bootstrap, kept outside it so bootstrap does not have one, and outside any harness, so a bootstrap release never waits on a harness that depends on bootstrap. A SIBLING, never nested in bootstrap, because nesting would put .ts inside the tree a Bootstrapping Agent is told holds none. It depends on bootstrap and on nothing above it — `check:closure` fails on any import that leaves it. It is ONE toolset over swappable content: someone who wants a different visualiser or generator uses a different toolset against the same bootstrap.
name: bootstrap-tools
title: Bootstrap tools
description: The Zod source of bootstrap's schemas, the generators that write bootstrap's JSON Schemas, schema page and READMEs, and the checks bootstrap's content must pass — runnable by an agent, with zod, liquidjs, Playwright and bpmn-js as its dependencies.
_needs_comment: The one layer below it. It reads and writes bootstrap; bootstrap never imports from here.
_supports_comment: Which content versions these tools handle, as a list of supported MAJOR versions per content graph — never a range expression. Within one major a newer minor or patch only adds. Each repository is versioned on its own, and a tools release may support several content majors. A tool refuses a content major not listed here rather than guessing. `bootstrap-tools` is listed too: the toolset carries a small content graph of its own (its processes, scenarios and skills), which the tools draw and describe like any other.

assets.title: AGENTS.md — bootstrap-tools
assets.description: The one-way boundary: this reads and writes bootstrap, bootstrap never imports from here, and nothing here imports above bootstrap. How an agent runs each tool, and what a Zod change does to a published contract.

assets.title: bootstrap-tools
assets.description: What the toolset holds, why it is outside bootstrap, and how to run it.

directories.title: Bootstrap's shapes, in Zod
directories.description: The Zod source of every schema bootstrap publishes, bootstrap's defined terms and graph typologies, and the small readers the tools share: a declaration reader over bootstrap's own shape, release addresses, and the declared-order check.

directories.title: The tools
directories.description: The schema generator and drawn schema page; the vocabulary, graph and named-subgraph exporters; the README writers (each directory's README, the `kg:processes`, `kg:files`, `kg:roles` and `kg:toc` sections, and the one-page README book) with their Liquid templates; the Process renderer; the site stager, publisher and push status; initialization; the release-IRI sync and the term linker; and the checks: import closure, node identifiers, bootstrap's concepts, bootstrap's documents parsed against their Zod (`validate`), and the semver bump the published schemas require, computed from a diff (`semver`).

directories.title: The toolset's skills
directories.description: The skills this toolset owns: `bootstrap-contract-semver`, what MAJOR, MINOR and PATCH mean for bootstrap's published schemas and why the bump is computed from a diff; `render-kg-to-github-pages`, rendering a Knowledge Graph (or a list of its Subgraphs) to GitHub Pages at a publication root URL and reporting the push's status with one message; and `github-pages`, the contract the host keeps.

directories.title: The toolset's Processes
directories.description: The toolset's own Processes, in bootstrap's diagram vocabulary: `render-kg-to-github-pages.bpmn`, rendering a Knowledge Graph (or a list of its Subgraphs) to GitHub Pages at a publication root URL, with each step one of these tools and the push's status and message as its output. The same process for a staging preview and a release; only the root URL differs.

directories.title: The toolset's Roles
directories.description: `roles.json`: the Roles the toolset's Processes bind their lanes to. The Site Publisher, who renders, deploys, checks and reports; and GitHub Pages, the host, acted upon.
